notes.front: Who is the station licensee of an amateur station?
notes.back: The person named in the station’s licence grant, who is responsible for the station operating properly under the FCC rules.
notes.explanation: Every rule about who answers for a station starts here: the licensee stays responsible even when someone else is operating.
notes.example: Like a car’s registered owner: the car stays in their name even when a friend is driving it.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is a station’s control point?
notes.back: The location at which the control operator function is performed.
notes.explanation: It is where the control operator is, not where the transmitter or antenna is; every station must have at least one (97.109(a)).
notes.example: Your antenna is on a hilltop, but you operate it from your desk at home: your desk is the control point.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is local control of an amateur station?
notes.back: A control operator directly manipulates the station’s operating adjustments to keep it within the FCC rules.
notes.explanation: It is the ordinary way of operating, and the baseline against which remote and automatic control are defined.
notes.example: You sit at your own transceiver and turn its tuning knob yourself.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is remote control of an amateur station?
notes.back: A control operator indirectly manipulates the station’s operating adjustments through a control link to keep it within the FCC rules.
notes.explanation: The control operator is still in charge, just from a distance; the pool’s example is operating a station over the internet.
notes.example: Unlike local control, where you turn the knobs yourself, you run your home station from a laptop in another town.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is automatic control of an amateur station?
notes.back: Devices and procedures keep the station within the FCC rules while it transmits, without the control operator being present at a control point.
notes.explanation: Only stations the rules specifically designate may be automatically controlled; repeaters are one (97.109(d), 97.205(d)).
notes.example: A hilltop repeater re-sending other stations day and night with nobody at its controls.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Is an amateur station ever allowed to transmit without a control operator?
notes.back: No. Every amateur station must have a control operator whenever it transmits.
notes.explanation: 97.7 has no exceptions; even a repeater under automatic control still has a control operator, who just need not be at the control point.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Who must designate a station’s control operator?
notes.back: The station licensee.
notes.explanation: Unless the station records show otherwise, the FCC presumes the station licensee is also the control operator (97.103(b)).
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Whose licence class decides what frequencies and privileges a station may use?
notes.back: The control operator’s: a station may only operate within the privileges of the control operator’s licence class.
notes.explanation: The licence class of the station licensee, or of anyone else present, does not matter; 97.105(b) looks only at the control operator.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: When the control operator is not the station licensee, who is responsible for proper operation of the station?
notes.back: Both of them, equally.
notes.explanation: 97.103(a) makes the station licensee responsible, and says that when someone else is control operator, both persons are equally responsible.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Under which kind of control need the control operator NOT be at the control point?
notes.back: Automatic control. Under local or remote control, the control operator must be at the control point.
notes.explanation: 97.109(b)–(d) set this out for each kind of control; under automatic control the devices and procedures do the compliance work.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Which amateur stations may be remotely controlled?
notes.back: Any station.
notes.explanation: 97.109(c) says any station may be remotely controlled, as long as the control operator is at the control point.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: Who may be the control operator of a station communicating through an amateur satellite?
notes.back: Any amateur allowed to transmit on the satellite’s uplink frequency.
notes.explanation: No special class or certification is needed; it depends only on whether your licence lets you transmit on the frequency you send to the satellite on (97.207(c) lists the space-station bands).
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: What is a control operator as defined in Part 97?
notes.back: An amateur operator designated by the licensee of a station to be responsible for transmissions and FCC rules compliance at that station
notes.choices:
A) The person speaking or otherwise communicating messages over an amateur station
B) The person who is the licensee of an amateur station
C) An amateur operator identified in the FCC database as responsible for transmissions and FCC rules compliance at a station license location
D) An amateur operator designated by the licensee of a station to be responsible for transmissions and FCC rules compliance at that station
notes.choicesExplained: A: speaking over the station does not make someone the control operator; someone else can speak under the control operator’s supervision. B: the licensee and the control operator may be different people. C: the control operator is designated by the licensee, not identified in the FCC database for a location.
notes.explanation: The key word is “designated”: the licensee chooses the control operator (97.103(b)), who is then responsible for the station’s transmissions alongside the licensee (97.103(a), 97.3(a)(13)).
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: When may an amateur station transmit without a control operator?
notes.back: Never
notes.choices:
A) When using automatic control, such as in the case of a repeater
B) When the station licensee is away and another licensed amateur is using the station
C) When the transmitting station is an auxiliary station
D) Never
notes.choicesExplained: A: a repeater under automatic control still has a control operator, who need not be at the control point. B: the other licensed amateur using the station is its control operator. C: no kind of station is exempt from having a control operator.
notes.explanation: When transmitting, every amateur station must have a control operator; there is no exception (97.7).
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: Who may be the control operator of a station communicating through an amateur satellite or space station?
notes.back: Any amateur allowed to transmit on the satellite uplink frequency
notes.choices:
A) Only an Amateur Extra Class operator
B) A General class or higher licensee with a satellite operator certification
C) Only an Amateur Extra Class operator who is also an AMSAT member
D) Any amateur allowed to transmit on the satellite uplink frequency
notes.choicesExplained: A: no class restriction applies beyond privileges on the uplink frequency. B: there is no satellite operator certification in the rules. C: neither Extra class nor membership of any organisation is required.
notes.explanation: A station talking through a satellite is an Earth station, and a holder of any licence class may be its control operator, within the privileges of that class (97.209(a)). So the only test is whether you may transmit on the uplink frequency.
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: Who must designate the station control operator?
notes.back: The station licensee
notes.choices:
A) The station licensee
B) The FCC
C) The frequency coordinator
D) Any licensed operator
notes.choicesExplained: B: the FCC grants licences; it does not pick your control operator. C: a frequency coordinator recommends repeater channels; it has no say over control operators. D: another operator cannot appoint themselves; the licensee designates.
notes.explanation: The licensee answers for the station (97.103(a)), so the licensee chooses who operates it. The FCC presumes the licensee is also the control operator unless the station records show otherwise (97.103(b)).
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: What determines the transmitting frequency privileges of an amateur station?
notes.back: The class of operator license held by the control operator
notes.choices:
A) The frequency authorized by the frequency coordinator
B) The frequencies printed on the license grant
C) The highest class of operator license held by anyone on the premises
D) The class of operator license held by the control operator
notes.choicesExplained: A: a frequency coordinator recommends repeater channels; it does not set privileges. B: the licence grant does not list frequencies; privileges come from the licence class. C: only the control operator’s class counts, not the highest class of anyone present.
notes.explanation: A station may only operate within the privileges of the control operator’s licence class (97.105(b); the pool cites 97.103(b)).
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: What is an amateur station’s control point?
notes.back: The location at which the control operator function is performed
notes.choices:
A) The location of the station’s transmitting antenna
B) The location of the station’s transmitting apparatus
C) The location at which the control operator function is performed
D) The mailing address of the station licensee
notes.choicesExplained: A: the antenna may be far from where the operator controls the station. B: under remote control, the transmitter is elsewhere; the control point is where the operator is. D: a mailing address is a licensing detail, not a place of control.
notes.explanation: The control point follows the control operator, not the equipment: it is defined as where the control operator function is performed (97.3(a)(14)), so under remote control it can be far from the transmitter.
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: When the control operator is not the station licensee, who is responsible for the proper operation of the station?
notes.back: The control operator and the station licensee
notes.choices:
A) All licensed amateurs who are present at the operation
B) Only the station licensee
C) Only the control operator
D) The control operator and the station licensee
notes.choicesExplained: A: people merely present are not responsible for the station. B: the licensee is responsible, but not alone. C: the control operator is responsible, but not alone.
notes.explanation: When the control operator is a different person from the station licensee, both are equally responsible for proper operation (97.103(a)).
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: Which of the following is an example of automatic control?
notes.back: Repeater operation
notes.choices:
A) Repeater operation
B) Controlling a station over the internet
C) Using a computer or other device to send CW automatically
D) Using a computer or other device to identify automatically
notes.choicesExplained: B: controlling a station over the internet is remote control. C: a device sending CW for you does not remove the control operator from the control point. D: automatic identification is a feature of the station, not automatic control of it.
notes.explanation: A repeater may be automatically controlled (97.205(d)): the rules are met without the control operator at a control point (97.3(a)(6)).
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: Which amateur stations may be remotely controlled?
notes.back: Any station
notes.choices:
A) Only repeater stations
B) Only automatically controlled stations
C) Only digital stations
D) Any station
notes.choicesExplained: A: remote control is not limited to repeaters. B: remote and automatic control are different; neither is limited to the other. C: the rule does not depend on the mode used.
notes.explanation: Any station may be remotely controlled, provided the control operator is at the control point (97.109(c)).
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: Which of the following is an example of remote control as defined in Part 97?
notes.back: Operating the station over the internet
notes.choices:
A) A software defined radio (SDR)
B) Operating the station over the internet
C) Controlling a model aircraft, boat, or car by amateur radio
D) Earth-Moon-Earth (EME) communication
notes.choicesExplained: A: an SDR is a kind of radio equipment, not a way of controlling a station. C: controlling model craft means sending control signals to a model, not remote control of an amateur station. D: EME is a way of communicating, not a way of controlling a station.
notes.explanation: Operating a station over the internet is remote control: the control operator adjusts the station indirectly through a control link (97.3(a)(39)).
notes.sourceLicence: A · public domain

notes.front: How do local, remote and automatic control differ?
notes.back: Local: the operator adjusts the station directly. Remote: indirectly, through a control link. Automatic: no operator at the control point.
notes.explanation: Under local and remote control the control operator must be at the control point; under automatic control, devices and procedures keep the station compliant (97.109).
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: You sit at your own transceiver and turn its tuning knob. Which kind of station control is this?
notes.back: Local control.
notes.explanation: You are directly manipulating the operating adjustments at the station (97.3(a)(31)); through a control link it would be remote control.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)

notes.front: What is the difference between the station licensee and the control operator?
notes.back: The licensee holds the station licence and designates the control operator; the control operator is responsible for the transmissions.
notes.explanation: They are often the same person, and the FCC presumes so unless the station records show otherwise (97.103(b)); when they differ, both are equally responsible.
notes.sourceLicence: B · public domain (US government work, 17 USC 105)
